_what: Warm generation throughput of the local oMLX fleet on THIS machine. Our own measurement, not a published number -- deliberately so: no source publishes tokens/sec for a specific quantisation on a specific Mac, and that figure is a property of the hardware, not of the model. It is the axis `refer` does not have.
_why_it_exists: Quality and speed are anti-correlated across this fleet. A pick-or-drop decision computed from `refer` scores alone deleted the entire fast tier on paper.
_method: Per model: one cold call (load + generate), then 3 warm calls. temperature 0, max_tokens 250, one identical pinned prompt. Rate is the server's own usage.completion_tokens over wall-clock; the warm figure is the median. cold_load_s is the cold call minus its own generation time, so it is load alone.
🔴 _limits: ONE prompt shape, short (~120 tokens in). These characterise short-prompt GENERATION only.
The long-context jobs send very large prompts where prompt PROCESSING dominates and MoE models behave differently. Do not pick a model for those from this file -- it has not measured that regime.
n=3 warm reps on a deterministic local server. Low variance reflects determinism, not a characterised distribution.
Output capped at 250 tokens; `truncated_at_cap` says which rows hit it. A model that stops early is timed over fewer tokens.
Does not survive an oMLX upgrade or a machine change. Re-run after either.
